name: Great Lakes–St. Lawrence Lowlands

geo.extent: Southern Ontario and the St. Lawrence valley to the Gulf

description: Plain-like lowlands bordering the Shield on the south-east from Lake Huron and Lake Erie to the Strait of Belle Isle, covered by glacial deposits. The West Lowland is split by the Niagara Escarpment; the Central Lowland between the Ottawa and St. Lawrence rivers is rarely above 150 m except for the Monteregian Hills; the East Lowland includes Anticosti and small Gulf coast areas. Small in area but home to most of Canada's population and farmland.

subregions: West Lowland (southern Ontario, split by the Niagara Escarpment)
Central Lowland (Ottawa–St. Lawrence plain to beyond Québec city on the north shore; Monteregian Hills)
East Lowland (Anticosti, Mingan, Gulf of St. Lawrence fringes, Newfoundland coastal lowland)
attributes.ecozone_named_in_source: Mixedwood Plains (plains, some hills; mixed deciduous-evergreen forest; cool to mild, moist) – 168,000 km2
